task:
pp.match_previous_expr works only for the first pair in a parser's life. It fails on a second pair, on nested pairs, and after a failed parse. Packrat and left recursion are out of scope, as before.

Repeated pairs: take first = pp.Word(pp.alphas), second = pp.match_previous_expr(first) and expr = first + pp.Suppress(':') + second. pp.OneOrMore(expr).parse_string('a:a b:b c:c') must give ['a', 'a', 'b', 'b', 'c', 'c'].

Reuse after a failure: with that same expr object, call parse_string with parse_all=True on these inputs, in this order. 'd:d' must give ['d', 'd']. 'e:f' must raise ParseException. 'g:g' must then give ['g', 'g']. A failed parse must not affect any later parse.

Nesting: an inner match must pair with the nearest enclosing occurrence of the leading expression. Take:

LBRACE, RBRACE, SLASH = map(pp.Suppress, '{}/')
tag_name = pp.Word(pp.alphanums + '_')
open_tag = LBRACE + tag_name + RBRACE
close_tag = LBRACE + SLASH + pp.match_previous_expr(tag_name) + RBRACE
content = pp.Forward()
content <<= (open_tag + pp.Group(content) + close_tag) | pp.Word(pp.alphas)

With content.parse_string(s, parse_all=True), these must parse: '{a}xx{/a}', '{a}{b}xx{/b}{/a}', '{a}{b}{c}xx{/c}{/b}{/a}'. These must raise ParseException: '{a}{b}xx{/a}{/b}', '{a}{b}xx{/b}{/c}', '{a}xx{/b}'.

A leading match made on a branch that the parser later abandons must never pair with a repeat. All of these inputs must give the stated result when run in sequence on the same parser object.

Existing uses of match_previous_expr, including parse actions on the expression, must keep working.
